dustara.why: V2: the landing pad at the left end of the main road

ferrox.why: V2: the Relay Gate ring in Gate Plaza

sporeholm.why: V2: the landing circle on the giant mushroom cap

thalassa.why: V2: the compass landing pad on the Saltreach docks

neonis.why: V2: the landing ring on the starport deck

glyphos.why: V2: the jetty at Sunken Landing

pyros.why: V2: the iron landing pad at the left end of Cinder Hollow

glacia.why: V2: the landing pad under the glass dome

helix.why: V2: the docking bay pad on the Docking Ring

001.name: Your House 1F
001.notes: Hero's home ground floor: Mom's kitchen table, stove, TV, stairs up, door at bottom

t: Mom: Look at you two! Remember, if your Alienmon get tired, the Recovery Bay heals them for free.
Mom: And call home once in a while, Linker.
npcs.name: Mom
pre: Mom: Good morning, sleepyhead! Dr. Vashti called. She's waiting for you at her observatory lab.
Mom: It's the big dome with the telescope, across the plaza. Go on, your partner is waiting!

002.name: Your House 2F
002.notes: Hero's bedroom: bed, desk with game console, telescope at the window, poster of the Starfall, stairs down

003.name: Vashti's Observatory Lab
003.notes: Domed lab with a big brass telescope, three capsule pedestals for the starters on a table, computers, bookshelves

objects.why: Vashti's starter pods on the lab table

t: Dr. Vashti: The Starfall Crater glows purple again. Something down there is stirring.
Dr. Vashti: Bring me news from every world you visit. And take care of your partner.
npcs.name: Dr. Vashti

t: Lab aide: Dr. Vashti tracks every seedpod that fell twenty years ago. There are still hundreds unaccounted for.
Lab aide: The big telescope points at the Starfall Crater. It's been glowing purple again.
npcs.name: Lab aide
pre: Lab aide: Dr. Vashti has been waiting for you! She's by the pod table.

004.name: Dustmere Plaza
004.notes: Home town: hero's house, Vashti's observatory dome, Recovery Bay, shop, the bridge exit east, trading post south

t: Bram: Sola's always at the Trading Post. If she says she's waiting for you, she means a battle!
Bram: The drift grass crackles with blue sparks. That's how you know Alienmon are hiding in it!
npcs.name: Bram
pre: Kid: You're getting your first Alienmon today? Lucky! Dr. Vashti's lab is the dome with the telescope.

t: Mr. Abernathy: Honey rolls, fresh out of the oven! First one's free for anybody with a brand-new partner.
Mr. Abernathy: I've baked for Dustmere since before the Starfall. Never once burned a loaf. ...Well. Once.
npcs.name: Mr. Abernathy

t: Girl: This is my Pebblet! It's a rock. It's my best friend. Both!
Girl: When it's sleepy it rolls into the shade. When it's happy it rolls into ME.
Girl: DX-4 keeps wandering off toward the bridge. Pebblet follows him. I follow Pebblet.
npcs.name: Rock-girl

t: Linker: Press START to check your team. A tired Alienmon is a fainted Alienmon waiting to happen.
Woman: The shop dome sells Stasis Pods. You can't catch anything without them!
Woman: Weaken an Alienmon first. A full-health one just pops right back out.
Watchman: West of here is the landing pad. Ships only leave with launch clearance from a Keeper.
DX-4: Bzzt! Scout unit DX-4 online.
DX-4: The bridge crosses the canyon to the east trading post. Mind the lava falls!
npcs.name: DX-4

t: Dusty: Name's Dusty. I've lived on this rim since the Starfall.
Dusty: That crater past the falls? The seedpods came down hot as stars twenty years back.
npcs.name: Old Dusty

t: Kit: I'm keeper of the Shards now. ...Okay, I gave myself that job. But somebody has to!
Kit: Dad gave me his old welding goggles. They're too big. I'm keeping them.
npcs.name: Kit

objects.label: A ladder leads up to the attic.
A ladder leads up to the attic.

t: Nurse: Welcome to the Recovery Bay! Step up to the counter and I'll heal your team.
npcs.name: Nurse

t: Trainer: I come here after every route. Healing is free, so there's no excuse to push your luck.
Shopkeeper: Talk to me at the counter for pods and potions!
npcs.name: Shopkeeper

t: Shopper: Gels heal, Cure Spray fixes poison and burns. I always carry both.

007.name: Dustmere Bridge
007.notes: The humming canyon bridge (story: Zib's signal, M02). Long wooden-and-brass bridge over a deep canyon, glowing rune lamps

t: Hiker: Don't look down. That canyon goes all the way to the old lava falls.
Bridge keeper: This bridge was built by Ferrox steelworkers. Not a single rivet has slipped in forty years.

008.name: Trading Post
008.notes: Small outpost of stalls and a corral where Sola waits (M03 first rival battle)

objects.why: house door: Trading Post dome (shared Dustara home)
house door: Trading Post dome (shared Dustara home)

t: Snack trader: Battle snacks! Get your battle snacks! Roasted cactus nuts, still crackling!
Trader: Everything here came over the Molten Frontier on a cart. Prices reflect the danger!
npcs.name: Snack trader

t: Kid: The lemonade stand? That was... an accident. Mostly the lamb's fault.
npcs.name: Kid with a lamb

t: Miner: The Sunset Tunnel past the cactus gardens is the only way through to the Frontier on foot.
Drifter: Sola trains out back every morning. Tough kid. Even tougher partner.
Linker: Trainers on the trail will battle you the moment they spot you. Walk past them if you're feeling brave.
Referee: One-on-one! First partner who can't keep going loses! No hitting trainers, no fighting dirty!
Referee: ...And no knocking over my lemonade stand AGAIN.
npcs.name: Referee

t: Fenna: Spores, roots, a few mushrooms that hum. I trade them for anything shiny.
Fenna: Sporeholm grows mushrooms bigger than houses. Bigger than Dustmere, nearly!
npcs.name: Fenna

009.name: Rimwalk Trail Part A
009.notes: Canyon-rim route with drift grass, ledges you hop down, trainers

t: Hiker: The Rimwalk Trail hugs the canyon edge. Great view, terrible place to trip.
Birdwatcher: I've seen Alienmon with wings riding the thermals over the canyon.

010.name: Rimwalk Trail Part B
010.notes: Canyon-rim route with drift grass, ledges you hop down, trainers

t: Researcher: Different grass patches hold different Alienmon. Try them all!
Camper: If you're low on health, head back to Dustmere. Pride is not a healing item.

011.name: Cactus Gardens
011.notes: Maze of tall cacti and flowering succulents, drift grass, hidden items

t: Gardener: These cacti store water for months. Some Alienmon nest right inside them.
Explorer: The Sunset Tunnel is just east. Bring light, it's a maze in there.

012.name: Sunset Tunnel B1
012.notes: Sandstone tunnel to the Molten Frontier; lantern-lit, boulders

t: Miner: Watch your step. The lanterns down here run on crystal shards.

013.name: Sunset Tunnel B2
013.notes: Sandstone tunnel to the Molten Frontier; lantern-lit, boulders

t: Old miner: You can feel the heat from here. The Molten Frontier is right above us.

014.name: Molten Frontier: Tunnel Mouth
014.notes: Exit of Sunset Tunnel onto volcanic far side

t: Guard: Welcome to the Molten Frontier. Stick to the trails and stay off anything glowing.
Traveller: The ash trail east leads to Palm Isle and Port Ember. Rest up there.
Guard: You're entering the Molten Frontier.
Helix built their forge fortress at the top of the ridge. Watch yourself up there.
Miner: That tunnel runs all the way under the sea to Sunset Canyon.
The ground's been rumbling since Helix started digging.

015.name: Molten Frontier: Ash Trail Part A

t: Ash walker: The ash makes everything look grey, but the Alienmon out here are anything but dull.
Sporefolk: Even here, spores find a way. The red blooms feed on lava heat.

016.name: Molten Frontier: Ash Trail Part B

t: Nomad: Magma-types love the warm ground. Hydro moves cool them off fast.
Geologist: These vents breathe every few minutes. Count to ten and you'll see.
Bug Catcher Grub: Fire bugs! The hottest bugs! Battle me!

017.name: Molten Frontier: Palm Isle
017.notes: Tropical island with Recovery Hut, palm trees, turquoise water

objects.why: Palm Isle Recovery Hut (works like the counter)

t: Nurse Coral: Welcome to the Palm Isle Recovery Hut! Let me patch your team up.
npcs.name: Nurse Coral

t: Nurse Coral: Wait. Is that... R.B. No. 1? That's Wren's badge!
Nurse Coral: I was her apprentice at the Dustmere Recovery Bay the night the stars fell. She taught me everything.
Nurse Coral: You've got her eyes. Come here, let me patch your team up. For Wren.
Islander: Palm Isle is the only green spot for miles. The Recovery Hut here has saved a lot of Linkers.
Fruit picker: Try the fire-coconuts. Crunchy outside, molten inside.
Explorer: The hut here is a Recovery Hut. Rest up before you head into the lava fields.
Weaken a wild Alienmon with a Tether Pulse, shock it with a Stun Spray, then fire the transfer beam!
Pilgrim Sol: The island spirits test every traveler. Let's battle!

018.name: Molten Frontier: Port Ember
018.notes: Harbor village with the harbor Relay Gate (needs 2 Shards)

objects.why: Port Ember healing centre (shared Recovery Bay room)
Port Ember healing centre (shared Recovery Bay room)

t: Sailor: The Deep Sea Ferry leaves from the long dock. Only cleared Linkers ride, though.
Dock mechanic: Helix boats have been prowling the harbor. Keep your pods close.
Fish seller: Fresh from the ember sea! Well... warm from the ember sea.
Harbor guard: Port Ember's been a safe harbor for a hundred years. We intend to keep it that way.
Linker: Every Keeper you beat gives you a Signal Shard. Eight of them and something big happens. Nobody agrees on what.
Villager: Welcome to Port Ember, the last calm shore before the lava fields.
Mina: This hood? It's a shark. Obviously. The fish respect it.
Mina: Cast past the end of the boardwalk and wait. Something on Thalassa always bites back.
npcs.name: Mina

019.name: Molten Frontier: Long Dock
019.notes: Long wooden dock where the Deep Sea Ferry berths (M08 Sola's Choice scene)

t: Deckhand: Mind the gaps between the planks. The sea down there is hot enough to boil soup.
Squid Sailor: The ferry at the end of this dock sails to the Deep Sea Ruins.
Hop aboard whenever you're ready.

020.name: Molten Frontier: Ridge Path Part A

t: Climber: The Ridge Path climbs toward the Forge Gate. Helix guards everywhere up there.
Researcher Kel: Lava-forged Alienmon have incredible stats. Let me show you!

021.name: Molten Frontier: Ridge Path Part B

t: Scout: I saw Helix grunts hauling crates toward the fortress. Something's being built in there.
Wanderer: The paths wind down the ridge to the Forge Gate and the shuttle pad.
Wild Alienmon roam the trails between towns. Keep your team healthy.

022.name: Molten Frontier: Forge Gate
022.notes: Ystran Relay Gate to Ferrox, guarded by Forge Miner Dax

t: Forge worker: The Forge Gate opens toward Ferrox once you've proven yourself.
Gate guard: No clearance, no passage. Those are the rules.
Forge Miner Dax: The gate's mine to guard. Beat me first!

023.name: Molten Frontier: Fortress Gate
023.notes: Helix Forge Fortress entrance, Helix grunt guard

t: Refugee: Helix took the old forge and turned it into a fortress. We had to leave everything.
Helix Grunt: Halt! This forge belongs to the Helix Directive.
Helix Grunt: Run along, kid. Come back when you're a real Linker, and maybe I'll bother beating you.
npcs.name: Helix Grunt

t: Helix Grunt: Halt! This forge belongs to the Helix Directive!
Former Helix worker: Helix is finished. I just want to fix things now.
Grub: Psst. I used to work in that Forge. I know a way in.
Grub: Beat the grunt at the door, then find the control room terminal. The keycard is in there.
npcs.name: Grub

024.name: Molten Frontier: Lava Bridges Part A

t: Bridge tech: These lava bridges are cooled by pumps. If they stop, run.

025.name: Molten Frontier: Lava Bridges Part B

t: Linker: Almost at the shuttle pad. Ships to the far planets launch from there.
Technician: This dish relays every signal in the Frontier.
Lately it keeps catching a pulse from the Starfall crater. Same rhythm, every night.

026.name: Molten Frontier: Shuttle Pad
026.notes: Fortress Shuttle Pad to Helix Station

t: Pad controller: Shuttles leave when the board says so. The board says 'not yet'.
Helix deserter: I flew shuttles for Helix. Never again. Ask me nothing about the Director.
Strand: Helix shuttles fly from this pad straight to the Starfall Rift.
Whatever they're hauling out there, they don't want anyone to see.

027.name: Molten Frontier: Shadow Tunnel Mouth
027.notes: Dark tunnel mouth leading to Umbra

t: Lantern keeper: The Shadow Tunnel leads to Umbra. The dark in there plays tricks on you.

028.name: Molten Frontier: Magma Mines Gate
028.notes: Sealed glowing-red Ystran door to Pyros

t: Mine foreman: The Magma Mines run all the way down to Pyros' crust. Hard hats mandatory.
Ystran echo: ...the mountain's heart burns like Ystra's dying sun...
...the Magma Mines go deeper than anyone has dared...

029.name: Gate Plaza
029.notes: Arrival plaza around the Relay Gate

warps.label: the Relay Gate back to Dustara
the Relay Gate back to Dustara

t: Gate guard: Welcome to Ferrox. Mind the rails, the ore carts don't stop for anyone.
Porter: Everything that lands here gets weighed, stamped and argued over. That's Ferrox for you.
Traveller: First time on Ferrox? Rustvale is just east. Best scrap stew in the system.

030.name: Rustvale
030.notes: Shanty town of shacks and converted rail cars

objects.why: house door: Rustvale home (shared Ferrox Cabin)

t: Scrapper: Everything here is built from junk. Even the Relay Tower.
Rail hand: Alloy-types love the rail yard. Bring something that burns.
Kid: Hank's Alienmon are tough as old boilers!
Watchman: Helix suits were sniffing around the crane yard last night. Hank's not happy.
Old welder: Hank Briggs runs the tower at the end of Furnace Ridge. You'll need a Shard's worth of guts to face him.
Linker: Magma moves melt Alloy-types fast. Volt moves just bounce off.
Kit: Dad says I can fix anything except my own room.
Kit: My {kit} sniffs out loose bolts. It's better at it than me!
npcs.name: Kit

t: Nurse: Welcome to the Rustvale Recovery Bay. Step up to the counter!
npcs.name: Nurse

t: Miner: I patch up my Alienmon here after every shift. The nurse doesn't even charge for the soot.
Shopkeeper: Pods, gels, sprays. Talk to me at the counter.
npcs.name: Shopkeeper

t: Customer: Stun Spray is a lifesaver on the Scrap Route. Those junk-types hit hard.
Grub: Mind the parts. Half of these are holding the other half together.
Grub: Come back when you've seen a bit more of Ferrox. I might have work for you.
npcs.name: Grub

t: Scavenger: The Scrap Route is all junk piles and loose rails. Alienmon love hiding in the scrap.
Hauler: My cart threw a wheel. Again. Third time this week.
Hiker: Tall rust-grass is where the wild ones hide. Walk around it if your team is tired.
Drifter: The crane yard's next. Watch for falling crates.

036.name: Crane Yard
036.notes: Swinging cranes, container stacks (Crane Yard Brawl)

t: Crane operator: Three junkers keep jamming my cranes. Hank wants them taught a lesson.
Yard guard: No Helix allowed in this yard. Not after what they pulled last month.
Junk dealer: One Linker's trash is another Linker's treasure. Mostly it's just trash.
Shopper: I came for a bolt and left with a jetpack. It doesn't work, but still.
Ore trader: Ferrox ore powers half the ships in the system. Helix wants all of it.
Fortune teller: I see... a tower. And a man with a very large wrench.
Furnace worker: The heat up here peels paint off ships. Keep your Alienmon hydrated.
Guard: Ferrox Tower is just ahead. Hank Briggs is the Keeper. Good luck, kid.
Tower engineer: Hank's apprentices train on this floor. The Keeper waits upstairs.

objects.why: Keeper's dais in front of the crystal, challenged from (7,5)

041.name: Landing Bog
041.notes: Landing pad on a boardwalk in the bog

t: Dock tech: Ships set down on the pad here. Mirefen Village is just east along the boardwalk.
Bog hiker: Stay on the planks. The bog looks like moss, but it's mostly water and bad decisions.

042.name: Mirefen Village
042.notes: Stilt village of huts on mushroom stalks with rope bridges

t: Spore tender: Mirefen stands on stilts. When the bog breathes, the whole village sways a little.
Botanist: The mushrooms glow brighter near the tower to the east. Dr. Moor says they're listening.
Bog hiker: Toxin-types hide in the reed beds. Carry Cure Spray, or the walk home gets long.
Villager: The dome with the cyan cross is the Recovery Bay. Rest up before you head into the marsh.
Grandmother: My grandson swears he was lost in the Mushroom Maze for a whole day. It was an hour.
Pilgrim: I came to hear the Spore Choir at the pools. On still nights the spores hum in harmony.
Man in a white coat: Helix? Never heard of them. I'm just... sampling the mushrooms. For science.
Traveler: The Keeper here guards a Signal Shard. Climb her tower and she'll test you herself.
Nurse: Welcome to the Mirefen Recovery Bay. Spore-sick or battle-worn, we'll patch your team up.
Visitor: Healing here is free. Step up to the counter whenever your team is hurting.
Clerk: Stasis Pods, Cure Spray, the works. In spore season the Cure Spray sells out fast.
Shopper: Weaken a wild alien before you throw a Stasis Pod. Healthy ones just pop right back out.

045.name: Lantern Marsh Part A
045.notes: Marsh of glowing lanterns and lily pads

t: Botanist: Every lantern in this marsh is a living fungus. Don't pick them. They bite back.
Bog hiker: Wild aliens jump out of the reeds. Stick to the dirt paths if your team is tired.

046.name: Lantern Marsh Part B
046.notes: Marsh of glowing lanterns and lily pads

t: Spore tender: The Mushroom Maze is just ahead. Left at the glowing caps... or was it right?
Wanderer: Trainers watch the paths. Step into their line of sight and it's a battle.

047.name: Mushroom Maze 1F
047.notes: Maze of giant mushrooms (Lost in the Mist)

t: Lost hiker: I've passed that stone shrine three times. I'm starting to think it follows me.

048.name: Mushroom Maze 2F
048.notes: Maze of giant mushrooms (Lost in the Mist)

t: Mycologist: These bridges grow on their own. The mushrooms knit the planks back together each night.

objects.why: V2: the mushroom house by the Spore Pools

t: Pilgrim: Listen... the Spore Choir. The pools sing when the spores rise. Some say the tower answers.
Spore tender: The big lily pads hold your weight. Mostly. Hop across them to reach the tower path.
Lab aide: Dr. Moor's apprentices guard this floor. Beat them and the stairs to her lab are yours.
Lab aide: Beat Dr. Moor and she'll hand over Sporeholm's Signal Shard. Bring Cure Spray. Trust me.

052.name: Port Saltreach Docks
052.notes: Fog-bound docks, net sheds, stilt houses

objects.why: V2: the dock Recovery Bay (shared room)

t: PORT SALTREACH DOCKS. Sunny skies, clear water, and the best fish pies in the Kessler system.
Sailor: Welcome to Port Saltreach! The fog rolls in every morning, thick as chowder.
Dockhand: Helix boats were circling the harbor again last night. White coats, no flags. Shady.
Swimmer: Hydro types are everywhere here. Bring something with Volt moves and they'll fold fast.
Net-mender: The big dome up top is the Recovery Bay. Rest your Alienmon there, it's free.
Diver: Tall weeds on the coral bars hide wild Alienmon. The shallows are full of them.
Old salt: Thalassa's rings throw rainbows on the water at noon. Best view's from the lighthouse.
Fishmonger: Fresh catch! ...No, you can't catch it with a Stasis Pod. It's a fish. It's dead.
Sailor: Lighthouse is east, past the market. The old Captain's Log is still up there.
Shopper: Stock up on Stasis Pods at the docks shop. A weakened Alienmon is easier to catch.
Mechanic: Captain Marsh's tower relays signals for the whole system. Or it did, till Helix came.
Traveller: Keepers guard the Relay Towers. Win and they hand you a Signal Shard.
Harbor guard: Trainers on the routes will spot you if you walk into their line of sight. Be ready.
Storyteller: They say Anchorath sleeps under the sea arch, and the tide turns when it dreams.
Nurse: Welcome to the Saltreach Recovery Bay. Your Alienmon will be shipshape in no time.
Sailor: I come here after every storm. Even my Alienmon get seasick, believe it or not.
Clerk: Ahoy! Pods, potions, rope, bait. Everything a Linker needs before the coral route.
Shopper: Status cures are worth it out on the islands. Wild bites sting more than you'd think.
Captain's Log, faded: 'The arch woke again tonight. The water glowed blue all the way to the tower.'
The rest of the page is water-stained.
Keeper's aide: The stairs up top lead out onto the coral sand bars. Watch for the tide.
Lamp tender: This light guided the fishing fleet for a hundred years. Helix ships ignore it.
Beachcomber: The coral bars connect at low tide. Hop the bridges and you'll stay dry.
Swimmer: My Alienmon love the shallows. Low-level ones, sure, but they never stop splashing.
Castaway: Saw an old wreck off the south rocks. Nobody's dared dive it yet.
Sailor: Harbor Tower is past the sea arch. Captain Marsh doesn't go easy on anyone.

059.name: Sea Arch Cove
059.notes: Giant stone sea arch where Anchorath sleeps

t: SEA ARCH COVE. Quiet waters. Something very large sleeps beneath the arch. Please do not wake it.
Researcher: Readings spike under the arch at night. Whatever sleeps there is enormous.
Pilgrim: Walk softly here. The islanders leave shells at the shrines so Anchorath sleeps on.
Lookout: Helix divers were poking around the cove. I chased them off with a bucket.
Deckhand: Captain Marsh is upstairs. Helix ripped the core right out of this tower. She's furious.
First mate: The Captain fights with the tide behind her. Volt types might give you a chance.

062.name: Neonis Starport
062.notes: Floating landing deck with orange landing ring (rebuild at new scale)

t: NEONIS STARPORT - Deck 7. Mind the landing ring while ships are docking.
Dr. Vashti: The signal is clearer here. Neonis hears everything in the system.
Dr. Vashti: Keep going, Linker. Every Shard brings us closer to the truth.
npcs.name: Dr. Vashti

t: Dock tech: Ships land on that orange ring. Stand clear unless you like being flattened.
Dock tech: The whole deck floats on Volt power. If the lights flicker, hold onto something.
Courier: Deliveries are faster across the catwalks. Faster still if your Alienmon can fly.
Raver: First time on Neonis? The city never sleeps. Neither do I, apparently.
Port guard: Helix freighters docked here last week. Paperwork was clean. Too clean, if you ask me.
Signal researcher: Every Relay Tower picks up the same pulse, every eight seconds. Spooky, right?
Traveller: The dome with the cross is the Recovery Bay. It heals your whole team for free. Use it!
Mom: My son wants to be a DJ like Static. I told him to finish his homework first.
A holo-ad loops: a glowing jellyfish Alienmon drifts by. 'Stay charged. Stay bright. Neonis.'
Raver: The whole city hums with Volt energy. Feel it? That buzz in your teeth?
Coder: Every sign in Neonis runs on Alienmon power. They get paid in snacks. Good snacks.
Courier: The Arcade District is east. Trainers there love a surprise battle.
Tourist: Volt types hate ground moves. Remember that before you climb Voltspire.
Street vendor: Neon noodles! You glow for an hour after eating. Totally safe. Mostly.
Archivist: Signal Shards are said to resonate with each other. Collect them and listen closely.
Suspicious man: Helix? Never heard of it. I just... like dark uniforms. Move along.
Nurse: Welcome to the Neonis Recovery Bay! Step up to the counter and we'll recharge your team.
Raver: Three battles in a row at the Arcade. My Alienmon needed a nap. So did I.
Clerk: Welcome to the Neonis Shop! Stasis Pods, potions, all the essentials.
Shopper: Stock up before Voltspire. Static's team hits hard and fast.
GLITCH HUNT: static-y Alienmon flicker between the cabinets after dark. Bring Stasis Pods!
Gamer: High score on Star Saucer 3! ...Okay, second highest. A Coder beat me with a macro.
Repair coder: Glitchy Alienmon hide in the static. A weakened one is easier to catch in a Stasis Pod.
Courier: Trainers battle you if you walk into their line of sight. Fight, or sneak around them.

067.name: Broadcast Route Part A
067.notes: Route of antenna towers and cables (Pirate Radio)

t: Dish tech: These antennas relay DJ Static's show to the whole system. Someone keeps hijacking channel 9.
Hiker: The glowing grass is full of wild Alienmon. Keep a few Stasis Pods handy.

068.name: Broadcast Route Part B
068.notes: Route of antenna towers and cables (Pirate Radio)

t: Radio fan: DJ Static picked up a signal coming from the Starfall Rift. It repeats every 8 seconds.
Raver: Voltspire is just east. Static's apprentices guard the first floor. They're loud. Really loud.
Stage guard: Welcome to Voltspire! The Keeper waits at the top. Heal up before you climb.
Sound tech: Feel that bass? That's the reactor below us. Static tunes it like an instrument.

warps.label: the Deep Sea Ferry back to the Long Dock
the Deep Sea Ferry back to the Long Dock
the Deep Sea Ferry back to the Long Dock

t: Sunken gate: The carvings are worn smooth by the tide. Only one glyph is clear: a seed.
Archaeologist: Welcome to Glyphos! Mind your step, half this place is underwater at high tide.
Dig Camp is just east. They've got a Recovery Tent if your team needs patching up.
Ferry hand: The Deep Sea Ferry runs here and back. Nobody else is brave enough to sail these ruins.

073.name: Dig Camp
073.notes: Archaeologists' camp of tents and scaffolding

t: DIG CAMP - Glyphos Expedition. Keep to the marked paths. Do NOT lick the crystals.
Archaeologist: These glyphs tell the Alienmon's story. Read the murals and you'll see.
Rune scholar: Crystal-types grow in the old courtyards. They love the humming stones.
Pilgrim: The obelisks in Glyph Hollow hum when you carry Signal Shards near them.
Digger: We found a whole hall of murals past the Coral Ruins. Took us a month to drain the steps.
Archaeologist: Trainers out on the ruins will spot you if you walk in their line of sight. Be ready.
Camp cook: No shop out here, friend. Stock up on pods and potions before you ride the ferry.
Rune scholar: Some Helix folks came asking where the murals were. Wouldn't say why. I didn't like it.

074.name: Dig Camp Recovery Tent
074.notes: Recovery Bay as a large tent

t: Nurse: Welcome to the Recovery Tent! Step up to the pod and I'll heal your team.
npcs.name: Nurse

t: Archaeologist: Dust, damp, and angry Alienmon. This tent has saved my dig crew more times than I can count.
Wanderer: Tall grass grows thick between the ruins. Wild Alienmon hide in every patch.
Rune scholar: The glyph under that pool glows at night. I think the whole valley was once a temple.
Pilgrim: Weaken a wild one before you throw a Stasis Pod. A tired Alienmon is an easy catch.

077.name: Glyph Hollow
077.notes: Hollow of glowing glyph stones (Guardian Stones)

t: Guardian Stone: Its glyphs pulse softly, like a heartbeat. It feels like it is waiting for someone.
Guardian Stone: The carving shows a ring of stones around a sleeping seed.
Pilgrim: The Guardian Stones circle the hollow. Some say they still guard something sleeping.
Archaeologist: The glowing door up the steps leads to the Mural Hall. Go look. Really look.

078.name: Temple of Voices 1F
078.notes: Ancient Ystran temple (no Keeper), 3 floors (Song of the Chimes)

t: Pilgrim: This is the Temple of Voices. Long ago the bells up top sang every dawn.

079.name: Temple of Voices 2F
079.notes: Ancient Ystran temple (no Keeper), 3 floors (Song of the Chimes)

t: Rune scholar: Every floor has the same glyph in the floor: a seed with wings. Curious, no?

080.name: Temple of Voices 3F
080.notes: Ancient Ystran temple (no Keeper), 3 floors (Song of the Chimes)

t: Altar of Voices: Old chimes hang silent above the dais.
A line of glyphs: WHEN THE BELLS SING, THE GUARDIANS LISTEN.
Pilgrim: The chimes fell silent ages ago. They say a Chimelet's song could wake them.

081.name: Mural Hall
081.notes: Great hall of Ystran murals (M10b Vashti's confession)

t: Mural: A golden sun over a green world. Tall figures raise their arms to it.
The glyphs read: YSTRA. Home. The garden that sang.
Mural: A vast tree-mother, roots wrapped around glowing seeds.
The glyphs read: THE SEEDMOTHER. She gave her children wings of pod and light, and sent them far.
Mural: A dark tide swallows the stars one by one. A pale world sits in its mouth.
The glyphs read: THE DEVOURER. It does not hunger. It simply ends.
Rune scholar: Three murals. A home, a hunger, a mother. Read them left to right.
Pilgrim: If the murals are true, every Alienmon you've met is a refugee. Makes you want to be kinder.

082.name: Cinder Hollow
082.notes: Mining camp of timber shacks, brass furnaces, rope lifts

t: CINDER HOLLOW. Raised on the first ember seam of Pyros.
Below, someone has scratched: 'Dig deep, come home.'
The camp furnace. It has not gone out in forty years.
A brass plate reads: 'Lit by Old Basalt.'
Miner: Cinder Hollow sits on the richest ember seam on Pyros. Also the hottest. Mostly the hottest.
Smith: Magma-types temper their own hides in the vents.
Bring a Hydro-type if you plan to argue with one.
Cook: Nothing beats lava-baked rockroot. Crunchy outside, molten inside. Don't bite too fast.
Ash walker: The crater's light still flickers some nights. The old-timers won't look at it.
Old miner: Basalt saw the first pod land, you know. He's been Keeper longer than I've been alive.
Still climbs that tower every morning on those knees.
Traveler: The dome with the cyan cross is the Recovery Bay. Free healing, even for outworlders.
Camp watch: Helix suits came through asking about the deep shafts. We told 'em nothing.
Folks who ask about the deep shafts never want ore.
Kid: I'm gonna catch a Cindermole and ride it down the rail line!
Kid: ...Mom says no.
Nurse: Welcome to the Recovery Bay. We'll have your team patched up and cooled down in no time.
Miner: Took a cave-in on B2. My Bouldron caught the worst of it, bless him.
Clerk: Stasis Pods, burn salve, cooling tonics. Everything a Linker needs down the mines.
Smith: Heat-proof Stasis Pods? No such thing, kid. They all hold up fine down there.
Rail hand: Stay off the tracks when a cart's coming. The carts don't stop, and neither does the lava.
Ash walker: Wild Alienmon nest in the ember-weed. Stick to the dirt if you want a quiet walk.
Rail smith: The Deep Mines start past the east bend. Three levels down, and hotter every level.
Hiker: Trainers out here spot you from five paces. Eyes front, Pods ready.

087.name: Deep Mines B1
087.notes: Deep mines, 3 levels (Teo's Trail 1, Deep Drill)

t: Miner: Teo Reyes came down this shaft once, chasing some signal. Folks say his tracks go deeper than ours.

088.name: Deep Mines B2
088.notes: Deep mines, 3 levels (Teo's Trail 1, Deep Drill)

t: Geologist: These red crystals hum on the same pulse as the crater.
Signal Shards grow from the same rock, I'd bet my lamp on it.

089.name: Deep Mines B3
089.notes: Deep mines, 3 levels (Teo's Trail 1, Deep Drill)

t: Deep crew: Furnace Ridge is just above. No Recovery Bay down here, so heal up before you push on.
SHAFT 4 - CLOSED. Ember rain. Do not enter.
Volcano Tower: follow the ridge east.
Forge keeper: Every forge on this ridge was lit from the volcano's heart. Old Basalt lit half of 'em.
Pilgrim: The Volcano Tower is just east. Keeper Basalt waits at the top. He doesn't go easy on anyone.
Helix grunt: Nothing to see here. Just... surveying the ridge. Move along, Linker.
Tower guard: Basalt's apprentices hold this floor. Beat them and the stairs are yours.
Frostmark Research Station. The crystal in this fountain was cut from the glacier and never melts.
Founded by survey crews who came for the aurora and stayed for the ice.
Researcher: Something huge is frozen inside the glacier wall past the caverns.
We call it the Teeth in the Ice. Nobody sleeps well near it.
Climber: Ice paths are slick. Jump the cracks, don't walk them.
Aurora Route has frost grass. Wild Alienmon love it.
Radio tech: Our antennas pick up signals from the Starfall Rift.
Lately they pulse in sync with the aurora. Spooky, right?
Townsfolk: The Recovery Bay is the dome with the cyan cross. Heal before the caverns!
Guard: Helix crews keep asking for dig permits. The station keeps saying no.
If you see anyone in a Helix strand-suit near the fossils, tell us.
Wanderer: Keeper Ingrid lives up in Aurora Tower, past the Frozen Falls.
Win a Signal Shard from her and you'll have really earned it.
Mom: My kids want to catch a Cryo-type. I said only after their homework thaws.
Nurse: Welcome to the Frostmark Recovery Bay. Let's warm your team right up.
npcs.name: Nurse

t: Climber: Cold doesn't bother Cryo-types, but everyone else hates the caverns.
Heal here before you head out. It's a long walk back.
Clerk: Stasis Pods, gels, warm socks. Okay, not socks. Take a look!
npcs.name: Clerk

t: Researcher: I buy Stasis Pods by the crate. Cave Alienmon break out a lot.
Aurora Route. West: Frostmark. East: Crystal Caverns.
Warning: frost grass hides wild Alienmon. Keep a Stasis Pod handy.
Climber: Trainers spot you from a few tiles away. Step out of their line if your team is hurt.
Researcher: The aurora isn't just pretty. It carries a signal. We just can't read it yet.
Radio tech: The Crystal Caverns are ahead. Three floors deep, then up into the Fossil Dig.
Wanderer: Fire melts ice, they say. Bring something hot for Ingrid's team.

098.name: Crystal Caverns B1
098.notes: Ice caves with crystal icicles, 3 floors

t: Strand: (quietly) Keep walking. Pell's on the radio, and he notices everything.
Strand: Helix is digging under the Fossil Dig, toward the old Ystran bones. You didn't see me, and I didn't see you.
npcs.name: Strand

t: Pell: Hello again, Rook. This dig site is Helix business.
Pell: Helix doesn't lose things. We just collect them later.
npcs.name: Pell

t: Miner: These crystals sing when you tap them. Don't. The wild ones hear it too.

099.name: Crystal Caverns B2
099.notes: Ice caves with crystal icicles, 3 floors

t: Researcher: My Alienmon fainted in the cold once. Always carry a Revive Spark down here.

100.name: Crystal Caverns B3
100.notes: Ice caves with crystal icicles, 3 floors

t: The crystal wall looks almost like a wing... something huge is folded up inside the ice.
A scratched note: 'Fossil Dig is just above. Mind the stairs.'
Climber: The stairs above lead to the Fossil Dig. Look closely at those bite marks.

101.name: Fossil Dig
101.notes: Dig site with a giant Ystran creature frozen in the glacier wall (Teeth in the ice)

t: Frozen fossil site #1. A jawbone longer than a shuttle, gouged by teeth from something even bigger.
The bite marks are ringed with frost that never thaws.
Frozen fossil site #2. Ribs snapped clean through. The tooth marks are as wide as a road.
Field tag: 'Predator unknown. Size: impossible.'
Frozen fossil site #3. A thighbone with one huge crescent bite taken out of it.
Three sites, one bite pattern. Whatever ate these was the size of a moon.
The Teeth in the Ice: a giant Ystran creature, frozen mid-roar in the glacier wall.
Dig crews say it hums when the aurora is bright.
Dig chief: Three fossil sites, same bite pattern every time. Read the markers.
Digger: I asked Helix for better drills. They asked where the biggest bones were.
I didn't tell them.
Frozen Falls. The water froze mid-plunge, all at once, in a single night.
Locals swear a Glaciryx nests behind the ice curtain.
Pilgrim: The falls froze the night the aurora turned violet. I come here to listen.
Climber: Aurora Tower is just east. Ingrid trains Cryo-types up top.
Aurora Relay Crystal. It pulses in time with the sky.
Plaque: 'Keeper Ingrid Vale awaits challengers on the floor above.'
Relay tech: This tower boosts the aurora signal across the whole system.
Ingrid's apprentices will test you on the way up.
Researcher: Ingrid reads ice cores like books. She says the ice remembers the Devourer.

warps.label: the shuttle back to the Shuttle Pad
the shuttle back to the Shuttle Pad

t: The medical bay's scanner hums. Helix-grade nanites patch up your whole team.
objects.why: V2: medical module (cross) works like the counter

t: The medical bay's scanner hums. Helix-grade nanites patch up your whole team.
HELIX STATION - DOCKING RING. All personnel: report unregistered Linkers to Security.
Guard: Keep moving. Visitors aren't supposed to be on this deck.
Guard: Wait, are you a visitor? We don't get visitors. ...Carry on, I guess.
Helix grunt: I signed up for the free uniform. Nobody said it came with toxic cleanup duty.
Helix grunt: Don't tell Admin Vex you saw me napping by the planters.
Scientist: I just run the tests. Don't look at me like that.
Scientist: The medical dome up top heals anyone. Even intruders. Budget cuts hit the ID scanner.
Engineer: The power cores have been running hot all week. Engineering says it's 'within tolerance'.
Engineer: Containment wing is east. Then 2F, then Engineering, then Vex. Not that I told you.
Helix grunt: The cages? Oh, those are... wellness pods. For the Alienmon. Very relaxing pods.
Helix grunt: Toxin types love the green pools here. That's why we keep so many. Probably.
Guard: Labs are in the right dome, barracks in the left. Not that you're allowed in either.
Guard: Grunts spot you from five tiles out. Walk into their line and you WILL be battling.
Scientist: Stasis Pods work best on a weakened Alienmon. Helix just uses bigger cages.
Scientist: The Director keeps asking about Signal Shards. Why does a space station need Relay keys?
DUTY ROSTER: Shift A - cages. Shift B - cages. Shift C - also cages. Complaints to Admin Vex.
Off-duty grunt: This is my bunk. That's my bunk too. The new guy snores, so I took his.
Off-duty grunt: Lights out is at 22:00. Battles are at 22:01. Every night.
Barracks guard: Mess rule one: nobody sits in Admin Vex's chair. Rule two: see rule one.
SPECIMEN TANK 1F-03. Do not tap the glass. It taps back.
Lab tech: Those tanks hold Alienmon from every planet you've visited. We call it 'the collection'.
Lab tech: Upstairs is Project Rift. Downstairs is everything we can't explain to HR.
Scientist: Toxin types shrug off poison, but Gravity and Psi moves hit them hard. For science.
Scientist: Please don't free the specimens. I'd have to fill out so many forms.
PROJECT RIFT: stabiliser coolant at 81%. Director Thorne wants 100% by next cycle.
Senior scientist: The Rift engine needs a Singularity core. Admin Vex holds the only one aboard.
Senior scientist: Director Thorne says the Rift is a door. I've seen the numbers. It's a mouth.
Lab engineer: Don't touch the blue tank. Or the green ones. Actually, just admire from over there.
PROJECT UNITY LOG, Director Thorne:
"The Ystran prophecy says whoever reunites all her children lets the Seedmother grow again."
"So we will hold all of them. One of every species, in one vault, carried through the Rift."
"Whoever holds every species controls her power to regrow life. Then no accident is ever final."
CAGE CONSOLE: the Alienmon inside presses a paw to the glass. The lock reads HELIX ADMIN ONLY.
CAGE CONSOLE: something green shuffles behind the bars. The lock is keyed to an admin card.
Worried scientist: They cry at night. The Alienmon, I mean. I've put in for a transfer three times.
CONTAINMENT WING 2F. Toxin pools are for Alienmon conditioning. Do not swim.
CAGE CONSOLE: two tanks, two sleeping Alienmon. A sticky note says 'ask Bronn for the code'.
CAGE CONSOLE: status SEDATED. Someone has doodled a sad face on the screen.
Cage tech: Admin Bronn has the cage codes. He's been acting... odd lately. Almost sympathetic.
REACTOR CORE: output 340% of rated. A label underneath says 'it's fine'.
ENGINEERING LOG: Rerouted core power to the Rift engine again. Lights on 2F may flicker. - B.
Reactor tech: If the core turns white, run. If it's orange, that's normal. It's always orange.
Reactor tech: Vex's arena is straight up the corridor. Heal first. She plays dirty.
STAR MAP: every planet you've visited glows. One dark point beyond them all is marked RIFT.
Deck guard: Best view in the galaxy. Shame we only use it to watch for Relay Keepers' ships.
Helix grunt: Sometimes I come up here and wonder if we're the bad guys. Then payday comes.
A small crystal shrine. Travellers make a wish here before crossing the Wind Bridges.
SKYLINER HALO-1. Boarding by ticket only.
Today's departures: none. Enjoy the view!
Pilgrim: I rode the skyliner up from the cloud sea. My ears still haven't popped back.
Dock tech: The airships float on Psi-charged crystals. Don't ask me how. I just polish them.
Skywatcher: Skyreach Plaza is just east. Heal up at the Recovery Bay before the Wind Bridges.

115.name: Skyreach Plaza
115.notes: Plaza with holo-globe fountain (rebuild at new scale)

objects.why: house door: opens the shared Halo house

t: THE HOLO-GLOBE. Fourteen worlds turn in its light.
Look closely: one of them is slowly dimming.
Skywatcher: The islands float on updrafts. Don't look down. Seriously, don't.
Kid: I caught a Psi-type with a Stasis Pod! Weaken them first or the pod just pops open.
Star scholar: The Sky Temple sits past the Floating Gardens. Echo and Iris guard Halo's Signal Shard.
Nurse: Welcome to the Skyreach Recovery Bay. Rest your Alienmon, the thin air tires them out.
Visitor: Psi-types hit hard up here. Bring something sturdy, or bring plenty of healing gel.
Clerk: Welcome to Skyreach Supply! Stock up now, there's no shop past the plaza.
Shopper: I always carry spare Stasis Pods. You never know what drifts out of the clouds.
Bridge walker: The ropes creak, but they've held for three hundred years. Probably.
Pilgrim: Wild Alienmon hide in the pink blossoms. Step around them if your team is worn out.

objects.t: The shrine door is sealed. Old wind still whistles through the cracks.
objects.why: door plan: shrine door with no interior yet

t: Skywatcher: See those little islands drifting by? Some of them glitter with Signal Shard dust.
Mystic: The wind sings louder near the temple. The twins say it is singing your name.

objects.why: treasure chest drawn on the top-left ledge

t: GARDEN SHRINE. Leave the flowers, take the quiet.
The Sky Temple lies east, past the last bridge.
Botanist: These blossoms only grow above the clouds. Psi-types nest in them when the wind is calm.
Pilgrim: The Sky Temple is just east. Echo and Iris accept every challenger, but few leave smiling.

objects.t: The stairs are blocked off. You can't go this way.
The stairs are blocked off. You can't go this way.

t: THE SKY CRYSTAL. It hums softly.
For a moment you feel someone reading your thoughts.
Temple pilgrim: The twins wait upstairs. Their apprentices will test you first.
Mystic: One twin starts a sentence, the other finishes it. Don't let it rattle you.

objects.t: Loose rock blocks the passage.
objects.why: door plan: cave door with no interior yet

t: Traveller: You made it through the Shadow Tunnel? Most folk turn back halfway. Gravewell's just north.

objects.why: house door: opens the shared Umbra house

t: The Gravewell Lantern: lit the night the city tipped into the sinkhole. It has never gone out.
Scavenger: Gravewell was a city once, before it tipped into the sinkhole.
Now we just call it home and keep the lanterns full.
Lantern keeper: Keep to the lanterns. The dark plays tricks.
If a light goes out behind you, don't turn around. Just walk faster.
Drifter: Void-types only come out where the light can't reach.
The Sinkhole is full of them. Bring something that hits hard.
Old woman: The Recovery Bay is the brightest room in town. We go there to feel warm, not just to heal.
Researcher: The black-hole sky pulls on everything here. Even sound falls a little slower.
Helix contractor: Nothing to see here. Just... measuring the sinkhole. For safety.
Move along, Linker.
Kid: My big brother says the well whispers your name if you stand at the edge long enough!
Nurse: Welcome to the Gravewell Recovery Bay. We'll have your Alienmon glowing again.
Diver: I came up from Sinkhole B3 with every team member fainted. Heal before every level down.
Clerk: Lantern oil, Stasis Pods, potions. Everything you need to go down and come back up.
Shopper: Stock up on Stasis Pods. Void-types are slippery and slip out of a weak throw.

objects.why: house door: opens the shared Umbra house
house door: opens the shared Umbra house

t: Lantern keeper: Every lantern on this street is tended by hand. Miss one night and the shadows creep in.
Scavenger: Trainers on these streets watch from the dark. Walk into their line of sight and they'll call you out.

objects.why: house door: opens the shared Umbra house
house door: opens the shared Umbra house

t: Pilgrim: The Sinkhole is just east. They say a Signal Shard sleeps at the very bottom.
Drifter: Past the Sinkhole stands Gravewell Tower. The Keeper there fights with the dark itself.

129.name: The Sinkhole B1
129.notes: The Sinkhole, 4 levels (The well that whispers)

objects.t: This ladder is broken. You can't climb it.
This ladder is broken. You can't climb it.

t: Miner: B1's the easy floor. Mind the waterfalls; that glow isn't water.

130.name: The Sinkhole B2
130.notes: The Sinkhole, 4 levels (The well that whispers)

objects.t: This ladder is broken. You can't climb it.

t: Explorer: I've mapped this level three times. The tunnels never quite match my notes.

131.name: The Sinkhole B3
131.notes: The Sinkhole, 4 levels (The well that whispers)

objects.t: The stairs are blocked off. You can't go this way.

t: Researcher: Ghost and Void readings double every floor down. Whatever is below, it is awake.

132.name: The Sinkhole B4
132.notes: The Sinkhole, 4 levels (The well that whispers)

objects.t: The stairs are blocked off. You can't go this way.
The stairs are blocked off. You can't go this way.

t: Pilgrim: The well that whispers... listen. Do you hear it too?
Go around the rift. Never across.
Kade's Notes: 'Thorne knew. The engine does not open a door. It rings a bell, and something below is listening.'
A cracked Rift-engine prototype. The orb inside still turns, slowly, toward the floor.
Lab assistant: The professor left in a hurry years ago. The papers are still exactly where he dropped them.
A void crystal hums on the altar. Your shadow leans toward it.
Tower guard: Keeper Kade waits upstairs. Beat his apprentices first; he only sees challengers who've earned it.

objects.why: house door: opens the shared Starfall Rift house
house door: opens the shared Starfall Rift house
house door: opens the shared Starfall Rift house

t: A hand-lettered card on the stall: 'Closed until the Helix inspection is over. Again.'
CORDON NOTICE: Civilian access to the Starfall Rift is suspended by order of the Helix Directive.
Someone has scratched underneath: 'Since when does Helix give orders out here?'
Tamsin: The crater's three levels deep, and the light gets stranger the further down you go.
Tamsin: Thirty years I've looked for the world on my question-mark patch. Maybe it's down there.
npcs.name: Tamsin

t: Cordon guard: Nobody goes past the fields without a reason. Got one? Fine, just don't die down there.
Rig worker: Helix left half its drills running when they ran. You can hear them grinding at night.
Rift seeker: Can you hear it? The crater hums like a heartbeat. Louder every week.
Star watcher: Crystals here grow overnight. I measured one at breakfast and again at dinner. Twice as big.
Camp tech: The Medic Tent is the dome with the blue cross. Rest your team before the Seedpod Fields.
Old hand: Twenty years back the pods fell right here. Every Alienmon you've ever met came from that sky.
Ex-Helix grunt: I scratched the logo off my jacket. Whatever Thorne's building down there, I want no part.
Nurse: Welcome to the Medic Tent. Step up to the counter and I'll patch your team right up.
Injured driller: Got clipped by a crystal-type in the fields. Those shells hide more than dust, kid.
Researcher: Each cracked seedpod is a shell something hatched from. Rare Alienmon hide in the pink weeds.
Hiker: Out of Stasis Pods already? Weaken them first - a tired Alienmon is much easier to catch.

objects.t: The stairs are blocked off. You can't go this way.

t: Rift seeker: Trainers out here spot you from five tiles off. Heal up before you walk their line of sight.
Driller: Helix paid triple to dig here. Then the pods started glowing back. Nobody stayed for the bonus.
Teo's tent. The flap is tied shut with a careful knot, as if he meant to come back.
A child's drawing is pinned inside: a man, a star, and the word 'DAD'.
Teo's Journal, last page: 'The light at the bottom is singing. I think it knows my name.'
'If Sola ever reads this - I didn't leave you. I went to find out why they came.'
The campfire is long cold. Three cups still sit around it, one never used.
Pilgrim: They say an explorer camped here waiting for the light to speak. His tent still stands.
Wanderer: I leave a fresh cup by the fire each time I pass. Somebody should, for whoever comes home.
Lookout: Below, the Rift turns slowly, a purple wound in the crater floor. The hum is louder here.
Star watcher: Psi and Gravity Alienmon gather near the rim. Bring something sturdy.
Rim guard: The descent's three levels deep. Signal Shards resonate louder the farther down you go.
Caver: Watch the purple cracks. That's not lava, it's starlight. Doesn't burn - just pulls.
Helix tech (lost): My map says the Rift Engine is 'down'. Every tunnel here says 'down'. Help?
Pilgrim: The vortex below is breathing. If the Keepers' Shards ever meant anything, it's here.

145.name: Rift Engine Platform
145.notes: Helix Rift Engine platform (M19 Thorne at the Rift)

objects.why: house door: opens the shared Starfall Rift house
house door: path in front opened to match the drawn ground

t: RIFT ENGINE CONSOLE - Containment field: 41%. Output: rising. Authorized by Director K. Thorne.
Helix grunt: The Director's up at the Engine. Go ahead - I'm not paid enough to stand between you two.
Shaken scientist: Containment keeps dropping. That thing isn't a power source. It's a door.
SUMMIT UPLINK: Recovery terminal online. Last full heal before the Great Telescope.
APEX ARRAY. Lift gate: Observatory Halls of the Quorum. Road east: the Great Telescope.
Ace Linker: I beat the Quorum once. Then they beat me four times. Heal before every hall.
Astronomer: The thin air up here makes the sky so clear. On a good night you can see the Rift glow.
Summit guard: Only Linkers with all eight Signal Shards ride the lift. Go on, you've earned it.
CRYSTAL HALL, 1F. Seat of Quorum member Marisol Fenn.
Step into the orrery column to ride up to the Sonic Hall.
Ace Linker: Crystal types shrug off hits but crack under heavy blows. Bring something that hits hard.

objects.t: The stairs are blocked off. You can't go this way.
The stairs are blocked off. You can't go this way.

t: SONIC HALL, 2F. Seat of Quorum member Duke Harrow.
The dome hums a low chord. The right staircase climbs to 3F.
Astronomer: The dome here was tuned to hear radio stars. Now it mostly hears guitar solos.
PLASMA HALL, 3F. Seat of the silent Quorum member Saga.
A lone flame burns in the orb. The right staircase climbs to 4F.
Summit guard: Nobody has heard Saga speak. The battle does the talking.
GRAVITY HALL, 4F. Seat of Quorum member General Ostrander.
Beyond this hall, only the Prime Linker waits at the Great Telescope.
Ace Linker: Gravity moves hit like a landslide. Lighten your team and keep your Pods ready.

151.name: Great Telescope
151.notes: Prime Linker Orra's chamber under the Great Telescope

objects.t: The stairs are blocked off. You can't go this way.
The stairs are blocked off. You can't go this way.
The stairs are blocked off. You can't go this way.
The stairs are blocked off. You can't go this way.

t: Dr. Vashti: I've got the road, Linker. It's holding. Go and bring her home.
Dr. Vashti: Kessler's side of the Vortex is safe with me.
npcs.name: Dr. Vashti

t: Kit: The lens is Teo's crystal map, ground down layer by layer. Took us three weeks!
Kit: If this works, we're walking to another world. No pressure.
npcs.name: Kit

t: Summit guard: Prime Linker Orra Venn bonded the very first Alienmon. Show respect, then show your best.
STAR CHART: Every Linker world is pinned here, Dustara to Starfall.
One faint point past the Rift has no name, only a note: 'Ystra?'
Astronomer: Every Signal Shard you carried lit a world on these charts. Helix wanted the map for itself.
Archivist: Quiet, please. The star charts are older than the Linker League itself.

objects.why: house door: opens the ystra house (was a chat knock door)
house door: path in front opened to match the drawn ground

t: A banner bearing the Seedmother's crest. Stitched below: 'Every road home begins with a single seed.'
Ystran echo: I remember this place green. Look, the first moss is back on the Arrival Fragment!
npcs.name: Returning echo 1

t: Ystran echo: ...welcome home, children of the stars. Rest by the crystal. It still remembers how to heal.
Ystran echo: We were a voice once. Now we are only the echo, waiting for someone to listen.
npcs.name: Ystran echo

t: Rift walker: Every fragment here was one world, once. The bridges are all that hold the pieces in a line.
Rift walker: Don't look down. There is no down. There's just... more sky.
Seeker: The Alienmon you carry were born here. Watch them. They know the way better than we do.
Seeker: The domes are sealed. Whoever lived in them left in seedpods and never came back.
Ystran echo: The floating islands are putting down roots again. Terravox hums when it walks.
npcs.name: Returning echo 2

t: Rift walker: The continents drift a hand's width a day. Cross the bridges while they still meet.
Rift walker: Gravity types love it out here. Everything floats a little, even your thoughts.
Ystran echo: Terravox carried a forest on its back... these islands were its footsteps.
Ystran echo: ...do you hear the roots? They are still reaching for each other.
Seeker: I came for answers. I found waterfalls that fall forever and never land.
Seeker: Wild Alienmon here are strong. Weaken them first, then throw a Stasis Pod.
Rift walker: The trainers out here are postgame tough. Heal at the Arrival crystal if you're running low.
A drowned archway. Aquelion, Pillar of the Seas, once sang the tides through this gate.
Ystran echo: Coral is growing in the Drowned Seas. Aquelion says the dreams are happier.
npcs.name: Returning echo 3

t: Ystran echo: These were our seas. Aquelion sang over them... now the water drowns the old roads.
Ystran echo: ...the coral still grows. Grief is not the same as ending.
Rift walker: Hydro types thrive in the drowned basins. Bring something that hits them hard.
Rift walker: Stick to the sand paths. The water here goes down further than any sea should.
The Sun Forge. Ignarch, Pillar of the Sun, fed Ystra's red star from this flame until the very end.
Seeker: The Sun Forge. They say Ignarch kept Ystra's red sun burning from this very pillar.
Seeker: The heat here is old heat. It doesn't burn you. It remembers you.
Ystran echo: When the sun began to die, we fed it everything... and still it dimmed.
Ystran echo: ...go north, into the crystal halls. The light there was ours.
Crystal altar. Glyphs flicker: 'We sang our memory into stone, so the stars would know we were here.'
A sealed reliquary. Its light pulses slowly, like something asleep and dreaming.
Saga: This was the Choir chamber, where every Ystran sang together. It is an instrument, not a building.
Saga: Gather the echoes. They will come if you call them with the old song.
npcs.name: Saga

t: Kit: Saga's right. This isn't a building, it's an instrument! A big, broken, beautiful instrument.
Kit: Give me some time. I can fix this.
npcs.name: Kit

t: Ystran echo: The Choir chamber sings on its own now. Every note is one of her children.
npcs.name: Returning echo 4

t: Rift walker: Crystal Ruins. Every pillar is a record. Nobody alive can read them anymore.
Rift walker: Trainers lurk in these halls. Step into their line of sight and they'll challenge you.
A small shrine. A worn carving shows seedpods rising from a great tree into the sky.
The Archive Disc. Most of its records are dark. One still glows: a map of stars named Kessler.
Tamsin: I'm staying on Ystra. There's a whole map room of places nobody has found yet.
Tamsin: A capture isn't taking. It's asking. Same goes for a world, I think.
npcs.name: Tamsin

t: Ystran echo: ...this was a library. We sang knowledge into crystal so it would outlive us. It did.
Ystran echo: Beyond these halls, the forest sickens. The Devourer's shadow touched it first.

objects.t: The stairs are blocked off. You can't go this way.
The stairs are blocked off. You can't go this way.

t: Kit: My {kit3} can heal the blight, slowly, tree by tree. We'll stay and do this part.
Kit: Go on. We've got this. Nobody gets left, remember?
npcs.name: Kit

t: Ystran echo: The blight is gone. The little shadows sleep in the new leaves.
npcs.name: Returning echo 5

t: Seeker: The blight spreads from the void's edge. Leaves turn to glass, then to dust.
Seeker: Some Bio types here still fight the blight. Help them and they might follow you.
Rift walker: Keep to the path. The blighted brush hides wild Alienmon that strike before you see them.

objects.t: The stairs are blocked off. You can't go this way.

t: Ystran echo: ...the trees remember being green. If you listen, they will tell you what green sounded like.
Ystran echo: Past the void lies the Heartroot's crater. First, you must look into the hungry one.
Seeker: Eight Signal Shards held the Rift shut. Now you walk right through it. Strange, isn't it?

162.name: Edge of the Void
162.notes: Edge of the void where Oblivane waits

objects.t: The stairs are blocked off. You can't go this way.
The stairs are blocked off. You can't go this way.
The stairs are blocked off. You can't go this way.

t: A cracked pillar. Scratched in haste: 'It does not hate us. It is only hungry. Do not look into it too long.'
Rift walker: That's it. The Edge of the Void. Something in there breathes when the wind stops.
Rift walker: Save your strength. Whatever waits on that altar is older than the stars around it.
Ystran echo: The Devourer was never cruel... only hungry, and so very alone.
Ystran echo: ...if you face it, do not hate it. Hate is a kind of hunger too.

objects.t: The stairs are blocked off. You can't go this way.
The stairs are blocked off. You can't go this way.
The stairs are blocked off. You can't go this way.
The stairs are blocked off. You can't go this way.

t: A crystal shard from the Seedmother's old world-tree. It is warm to the touch, and hums the same note as your partner.
A quiet spring shrine. Seedpods once floated here before their long fall between the stars.
Ystran echo: Every child came home and stayed itself. That is the whole legend. Thank you, Unifier.
npcs.name: Returning echo 6

t: Ystran echo: Her world-tree stood here once. Every seedpod that crossed the stars was a piece of her. Now only the Heartroot remains.
Ystran echo: ...she is tired, Linker. But she waited for you. She always knew someone would come.
Seeker: I've walked every fragment of this world. This is the only place that feels like it is still alive.

164.name: Star Arena
164.notes: Floating coliseum among the stars: central battle floor, royal box with the Arena Master, vendor stalls left and right, south gate bridge

objects.why: the Arena Master at the top of the red-carpet stairs, below the royal box

t: Arena Master: Welcome to the Star Arena!
npcs.name: Arena Master

t: Vendor: Pods and gels for the brave!
npcs.name: Vendor

t: Arena medic: Step up to the stall and I'll patch your team up.
npcs.name: Arena medic

t: Fan: I've watched every Singularity League final. Grand Champion Nyx Horizon has never lost here!
Kid: I'm entering the Stardust League with my Lv 12 team! Level caps make it fair for everyone.
Commentator: Stardust, Comet, Supernova, Singularity. Each league has its own level cap and its own Champion.
Old fan: Your team is healed before every round. Losing just ends your run, no harm done.
Scoreboard tech: The board remembers every Linker who clears a Cup.

165.name: Recovery Bay Attic
165.notes: Nana Wren's attic above the Dustmere Recovery Bay: trunks, baskets, the old R.B. sign

166.name: Reyes House
166.notes: Teo and Sola's home by the Trading Post

t: Sola: I made a cactus-berry pie for your mom. It's... a little burned. A lot burned.
Sola: It's weird having a normal day. Good weird.
npcs.name: Sola

t: The house is empty. A sign on the door says: Reserved for the Reyes family.
npcs.name: Moving box

t: Teo: I never saw a living Seedmother. Just the empty crater where she stood, and the Heartroot, a little dimmer every year.
Teo: Lumivex grew up near its light. It keeps watch on the roof now. It doesn't trust doors yet. Neither do I.
npcs.name: Teo

167.name: Ghost Ship Hold
167.notes: The hold of the drifting Helix freighter: empty cages and barred grates

168.name: Helix Freighter
168.notes: Helix cargo freighter at the east pier; Thalassa's tower core is held in the glowing cargo pit

169.name: Smuggler's Freighter
169.notes: A rusty smuggler's freighter at the Saltreach Market pier, where Admin Vex hides

170.name: Neonis Courtroom
170.notes: The Linker League courtroom on Neon Boulevard

171.name: Thalassa House
171.notes: Shared house interior: every house door on Thalassa opens here

t: Fisher: Mind the nets! I just mended them.
Fisher: On calm nights you can hear Gloopa singing under the piers.
npcs.name: Fisher

172.name: Starfall Rift House
172.notes: Shared house interior: every house door on Starfall Rift opens here

t: Rift Scout: Don't touch the crystals. They hum back at you.
Rift Scout: Every night the Rift glows a little brighter. I write it all down.
npcs.name: Rift Scout

173.name: Sporeholm House
173.notes: Shared house interior: every house door on Sporeholm opens here

t: Bog Keeper: Welcome, welcome! Shoes off, the moss is drying.
Bog Keeper: The mushroom lamps glow brighter when a happy Alienmon is near.
npcs.name: Bog Keeper

174.name: Pyros House
174.notes: Shared house interior: every house door on Pyros opens here

t: Miner: Long shift in the Deep Mines. Come in, it's cooler in here.
Miner: If your helmet lamp flickers, turn back. That's the rule.
npcs.name: Miner

175.name: Halo House
175.notes: Shared house interior: every house door on Halo opens here

t: Sky Weaver: The clouds drift right past my window. I never get tired of it.
Sky Weaver: Play the harp if you like. The wind shrines answer it, they say.
npcs.name: Sky Weaver

176.name: Neonis House
176.notes: Shared house interior: every house door on Neonis opens here

t: Night DJ: Oh, a visitor! Welcome to my studio. Well, my living room.
Night DJ: DJ Static lives three towers over. I've heard every set.
npcs.name: Night DJ

177.name: Glyphos House
177.notes: Shared house interior: every house door on Glyphos opens here

t: Dig Assistant: Careful with the scrolls, they're older than the city.
Dig Assistant: Those glyphs on the wall? Even Dr. Vashti hasn't read them all.
npcs.name: Dig Assistant

178.name: Glacia House
178.notes: Shared house interior: every house door on Glacia opens here

t: Grandma Frost: Come warm up by the fire, dear.
Grandma Frost: Ingrid used to sit right there when she was little.
npcs.name: Grandma Frost

t: Captain: Welcome aboard! She's docked for repairs, but the view's still free.
Captain: On a clear day you can see every island in the Halo chain from the helm.
npcs.name: Airship Captain

t: Prize Clerk: Welcome to the Neonis Arcade! The machines are being rewired for the big tournament.
Prize Clerk: Come back later and you might win one of those plush Alienmon on the shelf.
npcs.name: Prize Clerk

t: Field Scientist: Ystra was green once. Every sample we take says so.
Field Scientist: The crater readings change whenever a Linker walks by. Strange, isn't it?
npcs.name: Field Scientist

t: Dock Attendant: Welcome to the Cloud Dock. Airships leave when the winds allow.
Dock Attendant: Mind the windows, the sky islands drift closer than they look.
npcs.name: Dock Attendant

t: Dig Chief: Every glyph on that board came out of the ground this week.
Dig Chief: Whoever built these ruins knew the stars far better than we do.
npcs.name: Dig Chief

t: Greeter: Welcome to Sporeholm! Please don't step on the glowing moss. It bruises.
Greeter: The bog is safest on the lit paths. The mushroom lamps show the way.
npcs.name: Greeter

t: Mushroom Keeper: Oh! A guest inside my mushroom. Mind the jars, they're full of spores.
Mushroom Keeper: This mushroom was growing before my grandmother was born. It's still growing now.
npcs.name: Mushroom Keeper

186.name: Umbra House
186.notes: Shared house interior: every house door on Umbra opens here

t: Lamplighter: Come in, come in. On Umbra we keep every lamp lit, all night long.
Lamplighter: The Devourer follows the light, they say. So we never let it go out.
npcs.name: Lamplighter

t: Canyon Guide: Shoes off, the rug's my grandma's. Oven's always warm if you're hungry.
Canyon Guide: When the drift grass crackles at night, the Starfall Crater is glowing.
npcs.name: Canyon Guide

t: Scrap Welder: Every bolt in this cabin came off a crashed freighter. Hank says it's the sturdiest house on Ferrox.
Scrap Welder: Mind the stove. It runs on old reactor cores.
npcs.name: Scrap Welder

t: Crystal Keeper: These crystals grew from the old world-tree's sap. They still hum when an Alienmon walks by.
Crystal Keeper: Ystra was green once. Listen closely and you can hear it remembering.
npcs.name: Crystal Keeper

t: Moss Tender: The lamps are glowcaps. Pick one and it sulks for a week.
Moss Tender: Sit, sit. The tea is mostly spores, but the good kind.
npcs.name: Moss Tender

t: Old Netmender: You can see the whole bay from that window. Captain Marsh's boat comes in at dawn.
Old Netmender: If you hear singing under the pier, that's just the Gloopa. Probably.
npcs.name: Old Netmender

t: Late-Night Coder: Every screen in this place is tuned to DJ Static's channel. Rent includes the bass.
Late-Night Coder: The crystal on the table charges my phone. Don't tell the landlord.
npcs.name: Late-Night Coder

t: Ice Fisher: Fire's always lit. The blue flame burns colder than you'd think, but it keeps the frost off.
Ice Fisher: Ingrid digs fossils all winter. I just dig holes and wait for fish.
npcs.name: Ice Fisher
